Since it's built off of Chromium though, and Chromium is open source, you kinda know what's in it.

TL;DR:

Created by a founder of Opera.
A browser intended for "power users" (their words, not mine).
has many of Opera's lost features (they were lost when Opera moved to the Blink engine, which Chromium uses)
will have a sync platform one day (will not support Google Sync, but you can import from Chrome)
will have mobile version one day (that and sync are on the roadmap)
will have email client built into the browser
has the other following features:
* Tab Stacking/Grouping
* Side Panel (you can put web pages in it, effectively splitting your browser for 2 things at once)
* Note taking (easy as: highlight text -> right click -> create note. Which will create a note with the highlighted text, give it a timestamp and record the URL to the page it was on.)
* Mouse Gestures (hold right click -> draw an L -> Release right click -> closes current tab; do the same but with a reverse L and it will open a recently closed tab)
* Fully customize-able Keyboard Shortcuts
* A built-in Dark Theme
* A trash-can for recently closed tabs/windows

Plus more.
